message: Answered #114's open question: nothing sets this+0x28 = this+0x68 - the two bad outers are never constructed, they are raw slots from an alt allocation path
note: Ledger #115. No behaviour change - diagnosis only; probes stripped, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at reached 157 / callsites 437 / 274 kernel calls / 91 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs. CORRECTS #114: "the container is an embedded sub-object at this+0x68" is WITHDRAWN. The class is 0x64 bytes and its allocations are 0x68 apart, so "container == owner+0x68" was just the bump allocator handing out the next block. The real store is MEM32(esi+0x28) = sub_00222600(0) inside the factory sub_00222708, and probe PSTORE shows it SUCCEEDS on all seven objects that go through it (guard byte 0 every time), so "sub_00222600 returned NULL" is refuted. The two NULL-container outers 0x01098400 and 0x01098870 are NEVER CONSTRUCTED: probe PBASE inside sub_00216EE0 fired on exactly eight objects - those seven plus one STACK address 00F7FD98 - and on neither of them, and probe PCOPY in sub_0022229A fired zero times, yet their first word reads a valid vtable 0x003F5D88. Probes PC1/PC2 show all nine calls to sub_001F7930 come from sub_002235D0 (loc_0022379A, ecx = esi), where esi = MEM32(ebx) cached from sub_002226E0. sub_002226E0 has the same shape as sub_00222600: if MEM8(MEM32(0x5BC508)) == 0 it tail-jumps to the real factory, else it takes an ALT path through sub_00209650(0x2221E0) and sub_0020E520 on registry 0x5BC274. Probe PALT caught that path returning raw 0x68-stride slots once the guard is 1 - 00000000, 010982C8, 01098330, 01098398, 01098400, 010985B0, 01098870 - with 01098400 and 01098870 each immediately followed by the matching [PC2]. A trace watch at page offset 0 (the reliable regime) shows the guard at 0x01086000 flipped 0 -> 1 by sub_002366BC+0xB1, which is already in the crash backtrace at +0x14B, so the flip is a legitimate state transition and not corruption. The alt path is fully lifted - sub_002221E0, sub_002225B0, sub_0020E520, sub_00209650 all exist and none is stubbed - and sub_002221E0 is a descriptor thunk pushing (0x64 size, 0x219A10 ctor callback, 0x221F50, registry 0x5BC274, ...) into sub_002235D0, so sub_002235D0 is a generic parameterised type-registration routine. NEXT: sub_00219A10, the per-type ctor callback, constructs into a STACK buffer (esp -= 0x64; ecx = esp + 4; call sub_00216EE0) - exactly the lone stack construction PBASE caught at 00F7FD98. Work out whether the alt path's pool slots are meant to be constructed in place and by what; start at sub_0020E520 on registry 0x5BC274 and at how sub_002235D0 uses the 0x219A10 callback.

message: sub_002235D0 is a type-descriptor registration routine; the 0x219A10 callback is a vtable getter, NOT a per-instance constructor
note: Ledger #116. No behaviour change - diagnosis only; probe stripped, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at reached 157 / callsites 437 / 274 kernel calls / 91 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs. REFUTES #115's proposed next step. Full 11-argument map of sub_002235D0 recovered (esp -= 0x108 plus four callee-saved pushes puts arg_n at esp + 0x11C + 4n) and every slot matches what sub_002221E0 pushes: arg0=0 gates the callback, arg1=0x5BC274 is the get-or-create singleton cell, arg2=0x2264D0 and arg3=0x1A4340 are icalled, arg4=0x1F19C0 goes to +0x54, arg5=0x3F9734 is the type NAME copied by the strlen/rep-movsd block, arg6=0x64 is the instance SIZE stored at +0x48, arg7=0x219A10 is icalled ONCE at loc_00223721 with its return stored at +0x5C, arg8=0x221F50 is icalled if non-zero. So the object sub_001F7930 walks is a TYPE DESCRIPTOR, not an allocator instance. Probe PCB on the +0x5C store caught all nine registrations and the callback returns a VTABLE every time, with a different size per type (8, 0x64, 0x10, 0x44, 0x10, 0x14, 0x34, 0x50, 0x34): 01096BB8/003EEAE8, 01091AB0/003F5D88, 01097518/003EEED0, 01097728/003F7EA0, 01097498/003EEF28, then the four with cont28=0 - 01098398/003E0CC4, 01098400/003F7C90, 010985B0/003F7DB0, 01098870/003F79C0. That matches sub_00219A10's body exactly: it builds a throwaway 0x64 instance on the stack and reads one word back out at MEM32(MEM32(0x5BC508) + 0x394) - a "get this type's vtable" helper, which is all the stack construction at 00F7FD98 ever was. Self-consistent detail: the size-0x64 registration returns vtable 0x003F5D88, the class all nine descriptors belong to, so the metaclass registers itself - which is why the raw alt-path slots read 0x003F5D88 at +0 despite never running sub_00216EE0. sub_002235D0 does write name, size and the callback fields onto those raw slots; it simply never creates the +0x28 member container, because that is the factory sub_00222708's job via sub_00222600 and the alt path bypasses the factory. NEXT, narrow: sub_0020E520 on registry MEM32(0x5BC274), and sub_00209650(0x2221E0) - one of those must return a CONSTRUCTED descriptor once the guard byte is 1. Do NOT revisit sub_00219A10 or the twelve poolless allocator objects; both are settled dead ends.

message: Probed sub_0020E520: the generic create path never runs a constructor, and sub_00216FD0 is the writer that poisoned guest 0x8/0xC - #114's loop is closed
note: Ledger #117. No behaviour change - diagnosis only; probes stripped, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at reached 157 / callsites 437 / 274 kernel calls / 91 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs. sub_0020E520 -> sub_0020E547 is the generic "create an instance of type T": walk an override chain at MEM32(desc+0x3C), and when empty pick an allocator (desc+0x60 by name via sub_001E9B80 else default sub_001F5C20), allocate MEM32(desc+0x48)+MEM32(desc+0x20) through allocator vtable+0xCC, then call sub_002096B0(instance, desc). sub_002096B0 is NOT a constructor: it installs the vtable from desc+0x5C (the value #116's 0x219A10 callback produced), sets refcount 1, icalls vtable+0x50 - a two-instruction getter, sub_00216F70 for this class, sibling sub_00211480 in the same slot of vtable 0x003F4770 - and does allocator bookkeeping via sub_001E8E20 and vtable+0x160. So the instance is blessed and registered but never constructed, which is why the raw slots carry a valid vtable while probe PBASE proved sub_00216EE0 never ran on them. Probe PE520 at entry shows chain3C = 00000000 on ALL 15 calls, and sub_00216EE0 explicitly zeroes +0x3C, so the override path never runs and every descriptor born this way has +0x28 NULL. Probe PE547 right after the allocation ties it together: desc=01091AB0 reqsize=0x64 yields blocks 01098260, 010982C8, 01098330, 01098398, 01098400, 010985B0, 01098870 - exactly #115's PALT values - and desc=01098400, itself container-less, is then used as the descriptor for four more allocations of size 0x34, a half-built descriptor in live service. One allocation genuinely failed (desc=01097498 reqsize=0x10 block=0). CORRECTS #115: off20 is 0 everywhere, so the 0x68 stride is the allocator rounding 0x64 up, not a header offset. BIGGEST RESULT - #114's missing writer is found: sub_00216FD0, the inheritance step called from sub_002235D0, appends the parent's members through the CHILD's container with esi = MEM32(esi + 0x28) = NULL, doing MEM32(esi + 0xC) = count and MEM32(MEM32(esi + 8) + i*4) = member. That writes exactly the guest 0x8 and 0xC words sub_001F7930 later reads back as the fake element array and fake count, and explains why MEM32(0x8) changed mid-walk. Also noted: sub_0020E520's loc_0020E53B manual guard is DEAD - the original unguarded line still sits above it (#91 class) - and the function carries four duplicated copies of the same esi guard (#89 accumulation). NEXT: find what is supposed to write MEM32(descriptor + 0x3C); it is the single field separating a constructed descriptor from a raw one. sub_00216FD0 appending through a NULL container is a symptom, not the cause.

message: Nothing writes descriptor+0x3C, and it is not the missing piece - it is abstract-type redirection. Three candidate construction mechanisms eliminated; guard TIMING is now the lead
note: Ledger #118. No behaviour change - diagnosis and a negative result; probes stripped, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at reached 157 / callsites 437 / 274 kernel calls / 91 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs. NO WRITER EXISTS: 909 writes to +0x3C tree-wide but almost all are esp-relative stack locals; only 88 non-esp writes sit in the 0x001E0000-0x00240000 band, only 8 references to registry 0x5BC274 exist at all, and none writes +0x3C. Our type's setup thunk sub_00221F50 (arg8, icalled by sub_002235D0) only touches MEM8(ebp + 0x3C) on MEMBER objects. CORRECTS #117's framing: +0x3C is a type-REDIRECTION chain for abstract types - sub_0020E520 does `if (MEM32(esi+0x3C)) { call it; esi = result; repeat }`, gated alongside the abstract flag at +0x1A - so a directly instantiable type correctly has 0 there. The idiom exists elsewhere (sub_002263F0 stores 0x2263C0 into MEM32(0x5BC190)+0x3C) but not for us. FOUND THE REAL CONSTRUCTION HOOK AND IT IS STUBBED: sub_002096B0 tail-jumps to sub_002096FD, which calls sub_001EA5A0/sub_001EA600/sub_001EA6B0 then icalls vtable+0x24 and vtable+0x1C - the same two virtuals the bootstrap factory sub_00222708 runs after building the container. But reading the SHIPPED vtable out of default.xbe, descriptor class 0x003F5D88 has +0x24 = 0x0013D370 and +0x1C = 0x0015FDF0, both shared do-nothing stubs. Disassembly also confirms +0x50 is a getter not a ctor (0x00216F70 = `mov eax,[0x5BC274]; ret`, sibling 0x00211480 = `mov eax,[0x5BC498]; ret`), vindicating ledger #78's old note. THE PER-FIELD INITIALISER RUNS FINE: probe PINITF shows every new descriptor entering sub_001EA5A0 with valid inputs (desccont=01096B88, thiscount=0x1B, basecount=2, so 25 members iterated - exactly the 0x19 sub_00221F50 adds), and probe PHOOK shows all 25 member hooks resolving to just 0x0015FDF0 (no-op) and 0x001EB200, with NO failed icall. So "a missing member-init hook" is refuted and none of them builds a container. CASCADE MEASURED: instances whose descriptor IS the broken 0x01098400 show desccont=0 and a member count read from guest 0xC that varies per call (0x16, 0x16, 0x17, 0x2E), then dispatch +0x7C on page-0 junk - PHOOK caught mvt=000E8000 hook=84846850. One container-less descriptor poisons every instance of its type, another source of the 278 failed icalls. THREE MECHANISMS ELIMINATED: +0x3C redirection, the vtable+0x24/+0x1C init virtuals, and the member +0x7C hooks. The container is created ONLY by the bootstrap factory sub_00222708 via sub_00222600. NEXT, strongest remaining hypothesis is TIMING: the guard byte at MEM32(0x5BC508) is flipped 0 -> 1 by sub_002366BC+0xB1, and descriptors the real game would still build through the bootstrap factory are instead going through the self-hosted path. Investigate what sub_002366BC should have completed before +0xB1 and whether anything it depends on is inert in our port. Do NOT re-chase +0x3C, sub_00219A10, vtable+0x50, or the member hooks.

message: Guard flip is correct by design (timing hypothesis refuted); faithful found a REAL class-1 deferred-flag miscompile in sub_002366BC - fixed and kept, but proven unexercised
note: Ledger #119. No behaviour change and none expected - the fix sits past the crash point. Probe stripped, temporary stdio.h include removed, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at reached 157 / callsites 437 / 274 kernel calls / 91 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs. WHAT THE FUNCTION DOES: sub_002366BC is the bulk type-registration driver. It calls sub_00209650(0x2221E0) FIRST - registering the descriptor class itself while the guard is still 0, so sub_002226E0 tail-jumps to the real factory sub_00222708 and that descriptor (0x01091AB0) gets its +0x28 container - and only THEN does MEM8(ebp) = 1 at +0xB1 to switch the metaclass to self-hosting, before driving ~23 further type thunks (0x220870, 0x2361A0, 0x231820, 0x236280, 0x235FE0, 0x22B9E0, 0x2293E0, 0x22A0B0, 0x21EED0, 0x229360, 0x229260, 0x229F80, 0x22B850, 0x22F420, 0x22AC70, 0x22E3C0, 0x229960, 0x22DFC0, 0x230880, 0x2289E0, 0x2287E0, 0x21B7D0, conditionally 0x21EFB0). So #118's "the guard flips too early" hypothesis is REFUTED - the metaclass is fully built before the flip and the ordering is deliberate. ebp propagates correctly here: sub_0023666F reaches this fragment by TAIL JUMP, the one form that publishes g_seh_ebp, so class 4 is ruled out at this site. sub_00209650 is the dispatcher (`push edi; call [esp+8]`) and ALL 24 thunk targets plus 0x00227F50 and 0x002225B0 are registered - the manual-fix comment inside it claiming 0x00227F50 "has no recompiled function" is STALE. THE REAL FIND: faithful.py reports a deferred-flag miscompile at 0x002367CA, confirmed by disassembly - `cmp eax, ebx` (ebx is the zero register) then `pop ebx` then `jne`, while the lifted C re-evaluated CMP_NE(eax, ebx) AFTER POP32(esp, ebx), testing the restored caller value instead of 0. Intended: if MEM32(0x5BC220) != 0 skip, else register type 0x21EFB0. Fixed by evaluating into a local before the pop, comment at the site records the original instruction order. THIS MATTERS FOR THE TOOLING: ledger #56's "class 1 is CLEAN, zero sites remain" is WRONG IN SCOPE - that sweep and find_stale_flag_tests.py run over gen/recomp_*.c and this site is in recomp_seed.c. Re-run the class-1 tooling with recomp_seed.c included. HONEST CAVEAT: the fix is UNEXERCISED. diff_reached.py gives before 157, after 157, 0 gained / 0 lost, identical sets - and a probe at loc_002367C1 then fired ZERO times, so the branch is never reached because the boot crashes earlier inside the registration sequence this very function drives (crash frame sub_002366BC+0x14B). Kept on the #72/#90 precedent that provably correct changes stay even when neutral. STILL OPEN: post-flip descriptors still have no +0x28 container and nothing in the self-hosted path builds one. NEXT: probe the 23 post-flip registrations to find which one crashes, and whether it is the first type whose parent has members - sub_00216FD0 writing through a NULL child container is what poisons page 0.

message: Only ONE post-flip registration runs (sub_00220870); the boot dies in a nested one, sub_0021C110 - and the crash site is ARBITRARY, decided by page-0 state
note: Ledger #120. No behaviour change - diagnosis only; probe stripped, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at reached 157 / callsites 437 / 274 kernel calls / 91 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs, with #119's deferred-flag fix still in place. METHOD: one probe inside sub_00209650 (the dispatcher) printing MEM32(esp + 8) and the guard byte captures every registration in the boot - far cheaper than instrumenting 23 call sites. FULL SEQUENCE, 21 dispatches and that is all of them: guard=00 gives 002221E0, 002225B0, 00222230, 002221E0, 002221E0; guard=01 gives 00220870, 00227F50, 002221E0, 00227E00, 002221E0, 002221E0, 002221E0, 0021BD20, 002221E0, 0021BD20, 00221900, 002221E0, 0021BD20, 00222230, 0021C110, 002221E0. So only the FIRST entry of sub_002366BC's post-flip list (0x00220870) ever runs; the other 22 (0x2361A0, 0x231820, 0x236280, ...) never execute, and the remaining dispatches are nested dependency registrations pulled in from inside it. The boot dies in the last of those, sub_0021C110 - the final two dispatches are 0x0021C110 then a nested 0x002221E0 to mint its descriptor, then heap alloc #91, then the crash three log lines later. That matches triage's backtrace exactly, which carries sub_0021C110+0x12A directly under sub_002235D0. CORRELATION BY COUNTING, no extra run: the post-flip 002221E0 dispatches sit at positions 8, 10, 11, 12, 14, 17, 21 - seven - and ledger #117's PE547 measured exactly seven descriptor allocations off desc=01091AB0 at reqsize=0x64 (01098260, 010982C8, 01098330, 01098398, 01098400, 010985B0, 01098870), so the seventh and last is 0x01098870, the fatal outer from #114. THE REUSABLE POINT: the crash site is ARBITRARY. All seven post-flip descriptors are container-less and sub_001F7930 walks every one through a NULL +0x28; six survived only because guest page-0 word 8 happened to hold a plausible pointer at the time (#114 measured 0x01098468 for outer=0x01098400), and by the seventh that word had been rewritten to 0 so the junk walk landed on the real object 0x0120E000 and faulted. Do NOT chase sub_0021C110, sub_00220870 or the thunk ordering - they are downstream of the one defect. Also incidental confirmation that 0x00227F50 dispatches fine, so sub_00209650's comment calling it unrecompiled stays stale. SUGGESTED NEXT: run this exact path under the existing RECOMP_TRAP_PAGE_ZERO census build (build_page0.bat) - it would turn every silent page-0 read and write in this cascade into a precisely located fault in a single run.

message: Page-zero census: 1,072,484 page-0 accesses in one boot. sub_001186A0 alone does 1,048,599 walking a NULL node pool, stopped only by our own step-cap guard
note: Ledger #121. No behaviour change - the census is a separate diagnostic build (build_page0/), the normal build/ is untouched and still deterministic at reached 157 / callsites 437 / 274 kernel calls / 91 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs with #119's fix in place. Build exit status was checked explicitly BEFORE running the game (the #113 trap): BUILD_EXIT=0 and linked. THE CENSUS IS TRUSTWORTHY because it is behaviour-neutral, verified not assumed - page0_stderr.txt shows the same 157/437, the same 274 kernel calls and the same crash RVA 0xEADC61 as the normal build. TOTALS: 1,072,484 accesses (1,072,147 read / 337 write) across 177 deduped sites, 360 raw [PAGE0] lines. THE BIG NEW FINDING, and no prior ledger entry even names the function: sub_001186A0 performs 1,048,599 reads at just TWO instructions - rva=0x8298B0 (+0xE0) 524,300 reads of guest 0x184..0x1C8 and rva=0x8298DA (+0x10A) 524,299 reads of guest 0x180..0x1C4. It is a binary-tree search by node index (`edx = eax << 4; esi = MEM32(edx + ecx + 0x18)`, descending child indices at +0x10/+0x14 to the 0x3FFFFFFF sentinel) and its node-pool BASE ecx is NULL, so every node read lands in page 0. 524,300 is 2 x 0x40000 plus change, i.e. the walk runs to OUR OWN manual step-cap guard (`if (++_walk_steps > 0x40000u) bail`) on both calls. That guard's comment records it was added to stop "the quiet hang at 100 kernel calls" localised by the watchdog RIP capture at sub_001186A0+0xD6 - so the hang was real, the guard is scaffolding, and the census now names the actual cause. SECOND FINDING: sub_00209650 does 20,413 page-0 accesses - 19,390 reads of guest 0 at +0x22B and 1,022 reads spanning guest 0x8..0xFFC at +0x244. That matches its source: after the thunk dispatch it does `ebx = MEM32(edi + 4); eax = MEM32(edi); icall MEM32(eax + esi*4)`, so with a NULL base it takes the count from guest 4 and sweeps the ENTIRE 4 KB page as a function-pointer table, dispatching 1,022 junk targets - a large, previously unattributed contributor to the 278 failed icalls. THIRD: #117's prediction is now confirmed by instrumentation rather than inference - sub_00216FD0 shows 384 accesses over 6 sites all on guest 0x8 and 0xC, 64 each, including 64 WRITES to guest 0xC from +0x980 alone. That is the writer poisoning the words sub_001F7930 later reads back. message: Seeded sub_0011E13C - a generic g_esp+=4 stub was skipping `pop edi; pop esi`, destroying a caller's `this`. kernel_calls 274 -> 338, crash moves into the real construction path
note: Ledger #122. FOUND VIA THE PAGE-ZERO CENSUS, chased to a class-2b defect. CHAIN, every link measured: the census (#121) showed sub_001186A0 doing 1,048,599 page-0 reads. A probe inside its step-cap guard fired exactly twice with pool_ecx=0000016C and 000001B0 - NOT a NULL pool base as #121 said, but `NULL + 0x16C`, i.e. the OWNING OBJECT is null and these are two trees embedded in it (the arithmetic matches the census exactly: 0x16C + 0x18 = 0x184, and 0x1B0 + 0x18 = 0x1C8, the census maximum). The caller sub_0011E7A0 does `ebp = edi + 0x16C` with edi = this, so this == 0. Its caller sub_0011E980 receives a GOOD this - probe [PE980] entry this=005024D0, a static object - and by loc_0011EA02 probe [PL16C] reads this=00000000. Exactly ONE call sits between those two points: sub_0011E0F0. That function does `push esi; xor esi,esi; push edi; ...; jmp sub_0011E110`, so the matching `pop edi; pop esi` lives further down the fragment chain. sub_0011E110 branches `if (eax < 0x16) -> sub_0011E13C`, and sub_0011E13C DID NOT EXIST - recomp_stubs_unresolved.c:966 had `void sub_0011E13C(void) { g_esp += 4; }`. Disassembly of the original: 0011E13C `dec eax`, then the store loop, then 0011E14A `pop edi`, 0011E14B `pop esi`, `ret`. The generic stub returned immediately, skipping both pops, so the caller kept the zero that sub_0011E0F0 had xored into esi. Textbook bug class 2b. FIX: seed_missing_functions.py --va 0x0011E13C --apply (clean extent 0x0011E13C-0x0011E14D, 17 bytes, 8 insns; seeded C matches the disassembly instruction-for-instruction including both pops), plus replacing the stub line with the standard moved-to-recomp_seed.c comment to avoid LNK2005. MEASURED, deterministic 2 of 2: kernel_calls 274 -> 338, failed_icalls 278 -> 273, heap_allocs 91 -> 92, safe_stubs unchanged at 8. COVERAGE IS MIXED AND NOT GLOSSED: reached 157 -> 147, callsites 437 -> 421, set diff 6 gained / 16 dropped. The 16 dropped are the registration cascade and old crash path (sub_0021C110, sub_00221900, sub_00227E00, sub_0020A8B0, sub_00223EF0, sub_00221070 ...) - which #114/#120 proved were being reached BY DISPATCHING THROUGH PAGE-0 GARBAGE, so losing them is losing junk dispatch, not losing work. KEPT on the #72/#78/#89 precedent: the change is provably correct against the disassembly, and unlike #81 (which was reverted) it does not gain zero. THE CRASH MOVES INTO REAL TERRITORY: from sub_00205170+0x7D1 reading 0xFFFF0000 (a page-0 junk walk) to sub_001EA5A0+0x341 reading 0xFFFFFFFC, reached through sub_002096FD+0x70 <- sub_0020E547+0x375 - the actual construction path from #117/#118 - with a 26-frame backtrace. Four of the six newly reached functions (sub_00223F30, sub_00227DC0, sub_00227E40, sub_001F20F0) sit on that new chain, along with new frames sub_00214200 and sub_0021DB50. NEXT: the new crash is in the per-field initialiser sub_001EA5A0 with eax=0 and edi=0; and sub_0011E7A0's this is still NULL for a separate reason (the documented D3D-null pattern - the D3D/DSOUND/XGRPH library sections were never disassembled, so D3D-owned objects are permanently null and the documented remedy is a native shim in recomp_manual.c, not a deeper trace).

message: Probed the new sub_001EA5A0 crash: same NULL-container defect one layer deeper (inst = guest 0x8, count 0x18000001 from page 0). NEW lead - the descriptor container's count collapses 0x1B -> 0
note: Ledger #123. No behaviour change - diagnosis only; probe stripped, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at reached 147 / callsites 421 / 338 kernel calls / 273 failed icalls / 92 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs, #122's seed intact. Re-instrumented #118's PINITF site after the seed; 13 calls, tail: inst=01099468 vt=003F7C90 desccont=00000000 thiscount=0000001A; inst=011D0008 vt=00000000 desccont=00000000 thiscount=0000001A; inst=00000008 vt=00000000 desccont=00000000 thiscount=18000001. THE FATAL CALL: the "instance" is 0x00000008 - guest VA 8 itself being used as an object, MEM32(inst) reads 0 so it has no vtable - and with desccont NULL the member count comes from MEM32(0 + 0xC) as 0x18000001. The loop runs from basecount 2 toward 402,653,185, reading MEM32(MEM32(edi + 8) + esi*4) off a NULL container and dispatching vtable+0x7C on each; it survives 512 junk iterations and dies on the 514th. Every crash-dump register matches the probe: esi=0x202, ebx=0x18000001, ecx=0xFFFFFFFC, eax=0, edi=0, so `edx = MEM32(ecx)` on 0xFFFFFFFC is the faulting read. This is the SAME mechanism as #114/#118, just further along - the #122 seed did not change the defect, it let the boot reach a later instance of it. NEW AND SEPARATE LEAD, the cleanest one available: the descriptor class's own container 0x01096B88 stays a VALID pointer on every vt=003F5D88 row, yet MEM32(0x01096B88 + 0xC) reads 0x1B on the first call and 0x00000000 on all six later ones. Same container, same address, count wiped - so every descriptor-class instance after the first initialises ZERO members. That is not the NULL-container bug and it has a known precedent in #87/#88, where a container's count/array was zeroed because the array-grow path computed a capacity of 0. Writers to probe: sub_00209470+0x7C2 (the increment #87 traced) and sub_00202B87 (the grow). Do NOT use a trace watch on 0x01096B94 - page offset 0xB94 is the unreliable regime #114 documented; use probes at those two writers. Also visible: instances at 0x011D0008 and 0x00000008 both have vt=0, so objects are being manufactured from page-0 and near-page-0 values and handed to the initialiser as real instances. NEXT in order: (a) why the count goes 0x1B -> 0; (b) the still-unresolved descriptor +0x28 container from #117/#118/#120; (c) the D3D-null shim for sub_0011E7A0 per DEBUGGING_NOTES.md.

message: Ghidra ground truth settles the +0x28 question and refutes the zero-fill hypothesis; count flip bracketed to one window and the writer looks like a native memset, not guest code
note: Ledger #127. No behaviour change - diagnosis only; probes stripped, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at kernel_calls 338 / failed_icalls 273 / heap_allocs 92 / safe_stub 8, crash unchanged at sub_001EA5A0. FIRST SESSION WITH GHIDRA OPEN SINCE #125, which is what made the +0x28 half answerable. (a) CONFIRMED the +0x28 store exists in exactly one place: FUN_002226e0's pre-flip inline body does piVar1[10] = FUN_00222600(0) after FUN_00216ee0(piVar1); post-flip the same function returns early through FUN_0020e520 and neither call happens. Also note 0x00222708 is a mid-function label inside FUN_002226e0, NOT a separate function as prior entries imply. (b) NEW STRUCTURAL FINDING: FUN_00222600, the container builder itself, carries the SAME guard and also self-hosts through FUN_0020e520 post-flip - so both factories switch over, and what the generic path lacks is only FUN_00216ee0 plus the container build, NOT the vtable+0x24 / +0x1C virtuals (the pre-flip body calls those too, and sub_002096FD already does). (c) REFUTED my own hypothesis by measurement: sub_001EB200, the +0x7C member hook, is a zero-fill whose dest is instance + member[+8]; probe [PZERO] caught all 48 calls and every destination is inside the instance being initialised, none within 0x01096B88..0x01096B98. It is not the count writer. (d) Probe [PIEA] at sub_001EA5A0's ENTRY caught 14 calls where #123's inner probe saw 13 - a new earliest instance 0x010981B8 with cnt=0x1B - and brackets the flip between instance 0x01098260 (cnt=0x1B) and 0x01099050 (cnt=0), with zero member-hook activity in that gap, so the writer is outside this path. (e) Ghidra shows sub_001EA5A0 has THREE callers, not one: FUN_002096b0 plus FUN_001f7d30 twice, the latter reached from FUN_00204100 and never instrumented - that is the open lead. (f) INCONCLUSIVE, stated as such: a one-shot watch on 0x01096B94 caught one write from RIP=0x7FFAD2EAE579, which is a system DLL rather than our module (our RIPs are 0x7FF6xxxxxxxx), i.e. a native memset/memcpy; but the watch disarms on the FIRST write and the 0x1B->0 write is later, so this does not name the culprit, and trace mode is documented unreliable at this page offset (#114). If the writer really is a native memset in our runtime, this is a PORT defect rather than game behaviour. (g) Incidental: all 48 hook calls report len=003F0004, a code-region value in the high half, harmless only because the lifted code masks to LO16 = 4 bytes. Not a live defect, worth remembering.

message: COUNT WRITER FOUND: the container 0x01096B88 is itself default-initialised while populated - sub_001E9E60 memcpy's member 010976F0's default over inst+0xC with inst = the container. Unifies the count collapse with the +0x28 gap; refutes the port-defect theory
note: Ledger #129. No behaviour change - diagnosis only; all probes stripped, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at 338 kernel calls / 273 failed icalls / 92 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs, crash unchanged at sub_001EA5A0. THREE-STAGE BISECT, one build+run each. (1) Six probes across every label of sub_002096FD located the flip inside sub_001EA6B0 during instance 0x01098260: postEA600 cnt=0000001B, postEA6B0 cnt=00000000. (2) A probe after each member dispatch in sub_001EA6B0 showed the count holding at 0x1B through member 0x01097698 and reading 0 immediately after member 0x010976F0 (kind=00, member vtable 003F7C90); kind=00 selects vtable+0x68 and Ghidra reads MEM32(0x003F7C90+0x68) = 0x001E9E60. (3) sub_001E9E60 is the per-member DEFAULT-VALUE COPY - dest = instance + member[+8], source = member[+0x20], length = MEM16(member+0x14) - and a probe over all 55 of its calls found exactly one covering the count word: m=010976F0 inst=01096B88 off=0000000C len=0004, dest 01096B94..01096B98. THE INSTANCE IS THE CONTAINER ITSELF. Nothing is corrupt or mis-sized: member 0x010976F0 genuinely lives at +0xC, which is the container's count, and the hook correctly writes its default of 0. The wrong OBJECT is being constructed. TWO CORRECTIONS. (a) #123 filed the count collapse and the missing +0x28 container as separate defects - that is WRONG, they are one root cause: a post-flip descriptor has NULL +0x28 (Ghidra: FUN_002226e0 stores the container only in its pre-flip inline body), so construction falls back to the metaclass's shared container 0x01096B88 and default-initialises it, wiping the 27 members the bootstrap had installed. Fixing +0x28 should remove the count collapse for free; do not work them as two tickets. (b) #127 speculated this might be a PORT defect because the watch hit a system-DLL RIP - REFUTED. The lifter lowers guest rep movsd to native memcpy, so a CRT RIP is exactly what ordinary lifted guest code produces here, and proves nothing about origin. Read every future system-DLL watch hit that way. SCOPE NOTE: only 1 of the 55 memcpy calls lands on the container; the other 54 write genuine instances, so this is one mis-targeted construction, not a systemic mis-aim. STILL OPEN: the fallback site that selects 0x01096B88 as the object to construct has not itself been probed, and must be before any fix.

message: The container is reached by ESI CORRUPTION, not a fallback: a nested NULL-object recursion at member 0x01096FA0 leaves esp 20 bytes low, so sub_001EA600's epilogue restores esi = 0x01096B88. Corrects #129
note: Ledger #130. No behaviour change - diagnosis only; all probes stripped, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at 338 kernel calls / 273 failed icalls / 92 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs, crash unchanged at sub_001EA5A0. (1) CAUGHT DIRECTLY: probes at sub_002096FD's entry and sub_001EA6B0's entry show every pair matching except one - 096FD this=01098260 but EA6B0 this=01096B88. sub_002096FD keeps this in esi and does `ecx = esi` for all three calls, so sub_001EA600, called between them, failed to preserve the caller's esi on exactly that call. (2) sub_001EA600 is balanced on its face (pushes ebx/ebp/esi/edi, pops all four), so the fault is esp. Entry and epilogue probes: every healthy call shows in-out = 0x10, the bad one shows 0x24 - twenty bytes vanish, so the four POPs read the wrong slots and restore garbage. Classic "a stack leak is never local", damage landing in the caller's registers. (3) RULED OUT the runtime: RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE at recomp_types.h:674 does restore g_esp = saved_esp on every failure path, so the 273 failed icalls do not leak arguments. Noted in passing as a REAL but non-causal hazard: sub_001EA600's entry block captures _icall_esp BEFORE the four callee-save pushes, so a failure there would restore esp above the saved registers - wrong pattern, may bite elsewhere. (4) LOCATED: a loop-tail probe printing iteration, esp, edi and member shows it=02..0B clean at esp=00F7FC88 edi=01098260, then the iteration counter RESTARTS at it=00 with esp=00F7FC74 and edi=00000000 walking a NULL container - a nested sub_001EA600 entered from inside iteration 0x0B, i.e. from member 0x01096FA0's +0x74 hook, with this=0. (5) FULL CHAIN: member 0x01096FA0's hook -> nested sub_001EA600 with this=0 and NULL container -> junk page-0 walk leaves esp 0x14 low -> outer epilogue restores esi=0x01096B88 -> sub_002096FD calls sub_001EA6B0 on the CONTAINER -> sub_001E9E60 memcpy's a default over +0xC -> count 0x1B to 0. (6) CORRECTS #129: its claim that a NULL +0x28 makes construction "fall back" to the shared container is WRONG - there is no fallback path, esi is simply corrupted. The +0x28 gap is still real and a NULL object still triggers the nested walk, so they are related, but #129's "fixing +0x28 should fix both for free" is UNPROVEN. (7) PROCESS LESSON, second of this session and same family as #128: I read 30 lines of the loop trace, saw esp stable and concluded the leak was in the post-loop icall; the fuller trace showed otherwise. Confirm the tail before calling a region clean. NEXT: identify member 0x01096FA0 and why its +0x74 hook yields this=0. The esp leak and the count wipe are both downstream. Do NOT patch the memcpy, the POPs or the count.

message: THE +0x28 CONTAINER IS BUILT AFTER ALL - and the build FAILS. Member 0x01096FD8's hook sub_0020E960 calls FUN_0020e520(typedesc=01097498), it returns NULL, and the NULL is stored. Overturns #125/#127/#129
note: Ledger #131. No behaviour change - diagnosis only; probes stripped, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at 338 kernel calls / 273 failed icalls / 92 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs, crash unchanged. (1) A probe at loc_001EA621 printing each member, its +0x74 target, its field offset and the field value shows iterations 02..0B all targeting 0x0015FDF0 (the known no-op stub), and iteration 0x0C being the only real hook: m=01096FD8 tgt=0020E960 off=00000028. Offset 0x28 IS the container field, so the type system does carry a member that owns it and does give it a constructor. (2) CORRECTS #130's attribution: it named member 0x01096FA0, but that member's hook is the no-op and cannot recurse. #130's probe sat AFTER the icall so it printed the previous iteration - an off-by-one. The rest of #130 (the esi mismatch, the 0x24-vs-0x10 esp delta, the nested NULL walk, the runtime being ruled out) is unaffected. (3) sub_0020E960 is the per-member sub-object constructor: if member+0x34 is set it picks an allocator, calls FUN_0020e520(member+0x38) to CREATE the sub-object, and FUN_00209ec0 to STORE it into the instance. (4) THE MEASUREMENT: a probe right after that creation fires exactly once in the boot - made=00000000 memb=01096FD8 typedesc=01097498 inst=01098260. The creator returned NULL and the NULL was stored. That is the entire "+0x28 is NULL" phenomenon: not a missing code path, a FAILING one. (5) Descriptor 0x01097498 is the container type, cross-checked against #116's measured table (size 0x10) and against the pre-flip builder FUN_00222600 allocating its container at 0x10 bytes. (6) OVERTURNS #125, #127 and #129, which all concluded "nothing in the self-hosted path builds a container". They searched sub_002235D0, the registration routine; the container is built later, during instance construction, by the member hook sub_0020E960. The searches were right about where they looked and simply never covered this function - which is why four entries failed to explain the NULL. (7) It also explains #130's stack leak: FUN_0020e520 does not bail on a failed allocation, it blesses and constructs the NULL, and that nested construction is what walks page 0 and leaves esp 0x14 low. ONE failure, THREE symptoms: NULL +0x28, the esp leak, and the wiped count. NEXT AND ONLY QUESTION: why FUN_0020e520 returns NULL for descriptor 0x01097498. Per #117 it goes through sub_0020E547, which picks an allocator (desc+0x60 by name via sub_001E9B80, else default sub_001F5C20) and allocates MEM32(desc+0x48) + MEM32(desc+0x20) via allocator vtable+0xCC. Probe those. Do NOT hand-patch +0x28 - the builder exists and must be made to succeed.

note: Ledger #134. No behaviour change - diagnosis only; probes stripped, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at 338 kernel calls / 273 failed icalls / 92 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs, crash unchanged. (1) Recovered the dispatcher from the g_icall_trace ring buffer (a literal grep for +0x178 could never have found it - the dispatch uses a computed slot): this=01088A90 t1=00211280 t2=001E9380 t3=00216210. (2) sub_00211280 is the pool OPEN method and writes both fields #133 measured - it allocates 0x814 bytes via MEM32(DAT_005bb9ac)+8, stores it at in_ECX[0x1c] (= +0x70), zeroes all 0x205 dwords, and sets in_ECX[0x2b] (= +0xAC). (3) CORRECTING MYSELF MID-INVESTIGATION: I first read (2) as proving the id is "literally set to 1, so 4 is garbage and reading (2) is dead". Wrong - FUN_001f5d60 the registrar ends every path with vtable+0x164(flag + slot*2), so +0xAC is a legitimate REGISTRATION SLOT id and the twelve's 4 means slot 2. (4) sub_00216210 is the Alchemy/Intrinsic memory bootstrap: it strcmps a configured name string at DAT_005bc51c against "igArenaMemoryPool" and "igMallocMemoryPool", builds malloc(0xd0)/vtable 003F4770 or malloc(0xa0)/vtable 003F4DF8 accordingly, and loops 47 slots storing each at slot*0x90+0x14 - exactly the table sub_001E9380 reads back. (1) MEASUREMENT THAT NAMED IT: probing all four decision points of sub_001E8E20's registry walks for pointer 0x01098260 showed BOTH 0x01088A90 and the pool-less 0x01218000 answering owns=01 - impossible if the predicate works. (2) THE DEFECT in recomp_seed.c at loc_001FBAD7. Original x86 is the standard equality idiom: sub eax,esi / neg eax (CF = operand != 0) / sbb eax,eax / inc eax. The lifter emitted the negate with NO _cf assignment, and _cf is initialised to 0 at entry and written nowhere else, so the sbb always read 0, eax became 0, inc made it 1 - the predicate returned TRUE unconditionally. Reporting "338 -> 4000" would repeat the mistake that got #30 wrongly reverted. Judge this change on the set diff and heap_allocs, not on kernel_calls. message: Post-#136 crash PINNED to a DATA defect: the backward coalesce reads boundary tag 0x00001003 (size 0x1000 with flag bits 3 still set) at MEM32(esi-4), and the original does sub esi,ecx with NO mask - so esi lands misaligned at 0x010983F5 and every link after is garbage
note: Ledger #138. No behaviour change - diagnosis only; probes stripped, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at 4000 kernel calls (cap) / 274 failed icalls / 826 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs, crash unchanged at RVA 0xEAD9A1 = sub_00205170+0x7D1. (1) A WRONG FIRST GUESS, recorded so it is not repeated: I probed loc_002052CB after matching triage's "fault == edx + 0x0" to the bare MEM32(edx) there, and it fired ZERO times - that block never executes. Source-reading plus register matching is a guess; the probe settles it. (2) ALSO CORRECTED: I decoded guest bytes at guest VA 0x00205941 because triage said "+0x7D1", but that offset is into the NATIVE x64 build, not guest space, so the decode was meaningless. Resolving the RVA against the map's Rva+Base column (0xEAD9A1 - 0xEAD1D0 = 0x7D1) confirms triage was right; only my use of its offset was wrong. Guest and native offsets are not interchangeable. (3) THE MEASUREMENT, firing exactly once in the boot: [PCOA] esi=010993F8 foot=00001003 newesi=010983F5. That result is the crash dump's esi exactly, misaligned by 3. (4) THE LIFT IS FAITHFUL, checked before blaming it - raw bytes at 0x00205276 are 8B 4E FC (mov ecx,[esi-4]), 2B F1 (sub esi,ecx), 03 F9, 8B 0E, C1 E9 1F, C1 E1 03, 83 C9 04, with NO and/mask between the load and the subtract. The original expects a CLEAN size at [esi-4]. Do NOT add a mask here - that would be scaffolding over corrupt data. (5) 0x1003 is 0x1000 with the low three bits set. In a boundary-tag allocator the HEADER carries size|flags and the FOOTER carries the clean size, so this is a header being read where a footer belongs, or a footer never written, or a block boundary off by the header size. Everything downstream follows mechanically: bogus block, bogus tag, bogus links, MEM32(0x830C048B) faults. (6) WHY NOW: this is the first boot where the real allocator is exercised at scale (heap_allocs 92 -> 826 with #136), so the backward coalesce runs for the first time. The defect was always latent. NEXT: probe the WRITERS of the word at 0x010993F4 - either a free/split path writes size|flags where a clean size belongs, or the previous block never wrote a footer. The reader is proven faithful. The 184/217 recursion pinned at the logging cap is still unexplained; ordinal 217 is NtQueryVirtualMemory, which #33/#35 have history with.

message: The defect is UPSTREAM of the allocator: the fatal free is handed a "block" whose header word is a heap POINTER (0x01096C60), not a packed size|flags. The two healthy frees show real headers (0x203, 0x403) with PREV_IN_USE set. Corrects #138 - nothing wrote a bad footer; a non-block was freed
note: Ledger #139. No behaviour change - diagnosis only; probe stripped, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at 4000 kernel calls (cap) / 274 failed icalls / 826 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs, crash unchanged at RVA 0xEAD9A1. (1) One probe at the free path's entry decode caught all three calls in the boot: blk=01090004 hdr=00000203 foot=00000000; blk=01096DC4 hdr=00000403 foot=00000000; blk=010993F8 hdr=01096C60 foot=00001003. The first two are healthy - small packed headers with size in bits 5.. and bit 0 (PREV_IN_USE) SET, so the gate `test bl,1; jne` correctly skips the backward coalesce and neither reads a footer. (2) The third is NOT A BLOCK: its header word is 0x01096C60, a heap pointer. Bit 0 of an aligned pointer is 0, so the gate reads "previous is free", the coalesce runs, and MEM32(esi-4) returns whatever sits there - 0x00001003. (3) CORRECTS #138's framing: it asked who writes size|flags into a footer slot, but nothing wrote a bad footer - there is no footer there, because the thing being freed is not a heap block. Chasing footer writers would have chased a value that was never a footer. #138's other conclusions stand: the reader is faithful, the lift matches the original opcode-for-opcode, and no mask should be added. (4) 0x01096C60 sits among the type-system member descriptors this session has been tracing (0x01096B88 the metaclass container, 0x01096D20, 0x01096FA0, 0x01096FD8), so the word at 0x010993F8 looks like a link or element-array pointer of a live object - meaning an object interior, or something never allocated by this allocator, is being freed. (5) The free path runs only three times and only since #136 put the real allocator in service; the two healthy frees prove the allocator itself works. NEXT: find the CALLER that frees 0x010993F8 - probe sub_00205170's entry for the incoming pointer and correlate with the refcount-drop paths (sub_0020E960's tail decrements a refcount and calls free_object_instance at zero; sub_002041D0 is in the same family). Likely a refcount reaching zero on a non-heap object, or a free at an interior offset rather than a block start. Do NOT patch sub_00205170 - it behaves correctly given what it is handed.

Here I twice asked "who put this pointer there" without checking whether the container holding it was real. CHECK A POINTER IS NON-NULL BEFORE REASONING ABOUT WHAT IT POINTS TO - especially here, where mapped guest page 0 makes every NULL deref return plausible data instead of faulting. (2) SITE COUNTS across ~152 lines: sub_002041D0 38, sub_002235D0 18, sub_001F7930 14, sub_001EA730 12, kernel_thunk_dispatch 12, sub_0020E5A0 8, sub_001EA770 8, sub_00123490 8, sub_00209650 6, sub_001FBA90 4, sub_00011AB4 4, sub_0035ADA0 2. (3) sub_002041D0's accesses are a NULL-THIS FIELD PATTERN - it reads guest 0x0, 0x1, 0x4, 0x17, 0x20, 0x28, 0x2C, 0x30, 0x40, 0x50 and writes 0x2C, which are object field offsets rather than addresses. This sharpens #143's open discrepancy (entry ecx=4 and 0x17 versus subtraction esi=1): reads at 0x17/0x20/0x28 are exactly what this=0 produces, so some calls likely arrive with a genuinely NULL this. STILL NOT SETTLED - needs one probe printing entry ecx and subtraction esi in the same run. (4) NEW SEPARATE LEAD: a WRITE of guest VA 0 from sub_0035ADA0+0x3C, and 0x0035ADA0 is the D3D section base per DEBUGGING_NOTES.md - D3D-section code writing to page 0, fitting the documented D3D-null pattern. Not on the current crash path. (5) TOOLING, four failed attempts worth recording: build_page0.bat cannot be launched from the agent shell - cmd /c and cmd.exe //c both returned EXIT=0 having done nothing, and a backgrounded attempt sat alive ~20 min at 0.02 CPU with no compiler children and a 0-byte log, because vcvars64.bat blocks on stdin which the agent shell ties to null. FIX: a wrapper .bat redirecting every step from NUL, invoked via the PowerShell tool with a full path. LESSON: three separate exit-code-0 results were false passes; the only trustworthy evidence a build ran is the exe timestamp. That is #113's trap in a new form. Both the wrapper and this lesson are now in the page-zero-census memory. NEXT unchanged: find what calls sub_002041D0 with a NULL or small-integer this, and resolve the entry-vs-subtraction discrepancy with a two-point probe.

message: THIRD FIX: sub_001EA770 captured _icall_esp BEFORE its four callee-save pushes, so a failed vtable+0x50 icall rolled g_esp back past them and its epilogue handed the caller garbage - that is what turned sub_002041D0's esi from 0x17 into 1. Exercised (fault addr 0xF5FFFFFD -> 0xF6010013), coverage neutral. Also resolves #143's open discrepancy
note: Ledger #145. Deterministic 2 of 2 before and after at 226 kernel calls / 272 failed icalls / 95 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs; manual_edits 1066/1066 so the fix survives regeneration. (1) RESOLVES #143's OPEN DISCREPANCY: running both probe points in ONE build gives ENTRY this=00000004, ENTRY this=00000017, SUBTRACT esi=00000001 - two calls, and on the second esi CHANGES between entry and the subtraction. Neither earlier probe was wrong; esi was being clobbered inside the function. (2) SIX-POINT BISECT: esi is 0x17 at loc_0020421B, 0x17 at loc_00204222, 0x17 at loc_00204229, and 0x00000001 at loc_00204230 - and sub_001EA770 is the ONLY call between the last two. The lifted sub_002041D0 assigns esi exactly once, at entry, so the clobber had to come from a callee. (3) THE DEFECT: sub_001EA770's prologue pushes ebx/ebp/esi/edi and its epilogue pops them correctly reversed, so it looks innocent - but the generated code captured `uint32_t _icall_esp = g_esp;` BEFORE those four pushes and used it for the vtable+0x50 ICALL. RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE restores g_esp = _icall_esp on failure, discarding the four saved registers, so the epilogue's POPs read the wrong slots. (4) AND IT DOES FAIL: sub_002041D0 calls it with this = 0x17, so MEM32(0x17) reads mapped page 0, the vtable is junk and MEM32(junk+0x50) is not a real target. #144's census independently lists sub_001EA770 with 8 page-0 sites including guest 0x17 and 0x50. (5) FIX: move the _icall_esp capture to after the register saves and immediately before the call, with the original instruction order recorded in a comment. (6) MEASURED: reached 158 -> 158, all signals unchanged, diff_reached says "identical sets - the change moved no coverage at all". BUT IT IS EXERCISED, unlike #119: the crash fault address moves 0xF5FFFFFD -> 0xF6010013, i.e. esi now arrives as its correct 0x17 rather than the corrupted 1. Behaviour changed, coverage did not. KEPT on the #72/#78/#89 precedent. (7) It does not move the wall because the wall is a different bug - sub_002041D0 is still called with a small integer as `this`. (8) This is task B2's class and closes only ONE site; DEBUGGING_NOTES records the same defect at sub_00209650 plus 15 further candidate sites left unswept, and #130 flagged this exact pattern in sub_001EA600 as latent. The real remedy is translator.py's _fixup_icall_esp_save, which cannot distinguish an argument push from a callee-saved register save - still unfixed. NEXT: find what calls sub_002041D0 with this=4 and this=0x17; both calls in the entire boot pass small integers, so the caller is not passing an object pointer at all.

message: THE SMALL INTEGERS ARE CALLEE-SAVED CORRUPTION, and systemic: sub_002235D0's type-setup callback icall at loc_00223736 has FOUR of eleven callbacks failing to preserve esi - cb=002002B0 turns 01097498 into 4, cb=0021B890 turns 01098D08 into 0x17, plus two more that swap in other heap pointers. Nothing ever minted 4 or 0x17 as an object
note: Ledger #149. No behaviour change - diagnosis only; probes stripped, rebuilt, deterministic 2 of 2 at 226 kernel calls / 272 failed icalls / 95 heap allocs / 8 safe stubs, crash unchanged, manual_edits 1066/1066. (1) A five-point bisect across sub_002235D0 (loc_0022360D, loc_00223658, loc_002236B1, loc_002236EC, loc_00223736) found esi healthy at every one - all eleven values at loc_00223736 are real heap objects - while loc_00223738, the very next label, already carried 4 and 0x17. Between them lies exactly one thing: `if (MEM32(esp+0x13C) == 0) goto loc_00223738` else fall through to loc_00223736's icall through MEM32(esp+0x138), the caller-supplied setup callback (arg 8 per #116). (2) PAIRED PRE/POST PROBE, printed in full: cb=001EA570, 00219A10, 0021BAC0 and four calls with cb=0 all PRESERVE esi; cb=002002B0 turns 01097498 into 00000004, cb=0021B890 turns 01098D08 into 00000017, cb=001F3370 turns 01098638 into 01098728, cb=0021BB80 turns 010988F8 into 01098A68. Four of eleven fail. (3) SO THE PREMISE OF #143-#146 WAS WRONG: nothing ever constructs 4 or 0x17 and passes it as an object. They are simply whatever those callbacks left in esi. Two leave small integers and two leave other heap pointers - the latter are equally wrong and equally silent, and would corrupt a different object instead of crashing. (4) NOT ONE FIX: the four differ. sub_0021B890 does push esi in its prologue, so its loss is deeper - a callee, or an _icall_esp rollback of the #145 kind. sub_002002B0 never pushes esi at all and opens with `esp -= 0x10`, so either the original genuinely does not touch esi and a callee does, or its prologue is mis-lifted. (5) WHY NOW: sub_0021B890 and sub_0021BB80 are both among the eleven functions #142 newly reached, so this was unreachable before that fix. (6) FOURTH INSTANCE THIS SESSION of callee-saved corruption after #130, #142 and #145 - now the dominant bug class, with translator.py's _fixup_icall_esp_save still the generator-level suspect. NEXT: take the four callbacks one at a time, sub_002002B0 first since it produces the fatal 4 - probe esi at entry and every return path, and diff the lifted prologue/epilogue against the disassembly. Do NOT guard sub_002235D0's use of esi; expecting a callee to preserve it is correct.

message: Seed 512 data-referenced function pointers: the wall moves off sub_001FBA90 for the first time. Boot now dies inside static-initialiser call #3, sub_00239E50, the refcounted singleton that gates the type registry
note: Deterministic 2 of 2. Kernel calls 226->434. Coverage DOWN (callsites 437->415, reached 159->146, heap 95->92) and distinct ordinals FLAT at 17 - recorded as mixed, per the Phase B precedent where a dip was progress off garbage. Bisect of sub_00011E40 with per-call probes: calls 1 and 2 (sub_0011DD40, sub_001E8DE0) return; call 3 sub_00239E50 never returns. That function is operator new(0x3A0) + ctor 0x002154F0 + store to 0x5BC508; the ctor is a 182-byte leaf making zero calls, so the fault is in the allocation/registration below it, and the store to 0x5BC508 never runs - which is why every later reader sees NULL. Probes stripped and rebuilt before measuring.

message: Isolated the fatal call at sub_0020E547: of 11 calls to sub_002096B0, the first 10 are healthy and the 11th has adjust=[esi+0x20]=0xFFFFFFFF on object 0x01098358. The registry at 0x5BC508 is VALID (0x01086000) throughout - three earlier claims this session were wrong
note: REFUTES three of my own claims: (1) operator new(0x3A0) for the registry does NOT fail - probe [REGALLOC] shows it returns 0x01086000; (2) the store MEM32(0x5BC508)=eax is NOT skipped - it sits at loc_00239EA8, before the registration calls, not after them; (3) 0x5BC508 is NOT null at the crash - probe shows registry=01086000 on all 11 calls. The eax=0 in the crash register dump is the VALUE BEING STORED by 'mov [esi+ecx],eax', not the registry pointer, and I misread it as the latter. THE ACTUAL CAUSE, two faults combining: object 0x01098358 has -1 in its adjust field at +0x20 while every other object has 0, and the virtual call through [edx+0xCC] returns 0, so this = 0 + (-1) = -1. The caller guards with a zero-only 'je', which -1 sails through - a guard written for null does not catch a sentinel. Probes stripped, rebuilt, verified unchanged at 434/92/415.

message: Adjust=-1 is heap residue, not register corruption: the fatal descriptor 0x01098358 was never fully constructed. Field evidence shows the full ctor sub_00216EE0 ran on neither failing descriptor
note: REFUTES my own register-corruption theory for this field: sub_00216EE0 does 'xor ebx,ebx' at 0x00216EE1 before writing [esi+0x20]=ebx at 0x00216F32, so if that ctor runs the field is ALWAYS 0 - a clobbered ebx cannot produce -1 here. Probe [DESCFULL] compares three descriptors sharing vtable 0x003F5D88: 01091AB0 adj=0 f8=0 f1c=011D5008 f28=01096B88 (fully constructed); 01098550 adj=0 f8=FFFFFFFF f1c=0121D008 f28=0 (partial); 01098358 adj=FFFFFFFF f8=FFFFFFFF f1c=0 f28=0 (barely started). The full ctor sets +8 to 0, and both failing descriptors carry FFFFFFFF there, so it ran on neither - they came through the minimal path at 0x002222B5 which sets only +0x1c and +0x60 and leaves +0x20 untouched. ALSO SETTLED: the virtual call is not failing. Probe [VSLOT] shows slot 0xCC resolving to 0x001EC5E0, which IS lifted - it is one of the 512 data-referenced pointers seeded earlier today, so its 0 return is legitimate behaviour and adjust=-1 is the sole defect. Probes stripped, rebuilt, unchanged at 434/92/415.

message: Narrowed the -1 to a contradiction worth recording: the full descriptor ctor sub_00216EE0 runs on exactly 8 descriptors and NOT on the two failing ones, yet every static path that sets their vtable reaches that ctor unconditionally
note: Probe [CTORRAN] on sub_00216EE0 entry lists 8 descriptors (00F7FD98, 01091AB0, 01096BB8, 01097498, 01097518, 01097728, 010977C0, 01097858). The failing 01098358 and 01098550 are absent, and sit at HIGHER addresses - allocated after construction stopped. That confirms the ctor never ran on them, matching their +8=FFFFFFFF (the ctor writes 0 there). THE CONTRADICTION: only three sites write vtable 0x003F5D88 - 0x00216EFC inside the ctor itself, 0x002222B5 in sub_0022229A, and 0x00222729 in sub_00222708. sub_0022229A is unreachable this run (probe [REGFLAG] on its only entry sub_00222270 got ZERO hits), and sub_00222708 runs 'mov [esi],0x3f5d88' then reaches 'call 0x216ee0' with NO branch between. So an object cannot hold that vtable without the ctor having run, yet two do. Something outside these three paths is producing them - a memcpy/clone of a constructed descriptor is the leading candidate and is untested. ALSO RULED OUT: nothing writes -1 to any object +0x20; all 40 such writes in .text target [esp+0x20], which are SEH scope slots. The -1 is residue in memory never written, not a sentinel. Probes stripped, rebuilt, unchanged at 434/92/415.

message: The two failing descriptors are created by NONE of the three vtable-writing sites: sub_00222708 makes 7 objects and the ctor runs on all 7, sub_0022229A runs zero times, and neither failing object appears in either list
note: Paired probes [NEWDESC] on sub_00222708's post-allocation point and [CTORON] on sub_00216EE0 entry. Created: 01091AB0 01096BB8 01097498 01097518 01097728 010977C0 01097858. Constructed: the same 7 plus 00F7FD98 (a stack object from sub_00219A10, the other ctor caller). The failing 01098358 and 01098550 are in neither list, so they carry vtable 0x003F5D88 without passing through any instruction that writes it. Leading hypothesis is now a memcpy/clone of a constructed descriptor, or esi pointing into a larger structure that embeds one - both untested. ALSO CORRECTED: I earlier reported sub_0019F196 as 'not lifted'. It is hand-written in recomp_manual.c as 'static void' and registered at recomp_lookup_manual line 3835; my grep for '^void' missed the static. The backtrace confirms it runs, and gives the full boot chain in one frame list: sub_001A1C97 -> sub_0019F22E -> sub_0019F196 -> sub_001A1C23 -> sub_00011E40 -> sub_00239E50 -> sub_0023666F -> sub_002366BC -> sub_00209650 -> sub_002221E0 -> sub_002235D0 -> sub_00222708. Probes stripped, rebuilt, unchanged at 434/92/415.

message: Traced the fatal descriptor to its origin: it is not constructed at all. sub_0020E520 follows a forwarding chain through 'call [desc+0x3c]' and the returned object is what carries adjust=-1
note: Full chain now closed. sub_002226E0 is lookup-or-create gated on the registry ready flag at [0x5BC508]+0: probe [LOOKUP] over 13 calls shows 7 with flag=00 taking the CREATE path (matching exactly the 7 objects sub_00222708 built) and 6 with flag=01 taking the LOOKUP path once the table at 0x5BC274 is populated. The lookup calls sub_0020E520, which does 'mov esi,ecx; mov eax,[esi+0x3c]; call eax; mov esi,eax' in a loop, so esi becomes whatever the forwarding function returns - and THAT is the object with adjust=-1. It never passes any of the three vtable-writing instructions, which is why probes at both the ctor entry and its vtable store list 8 objects and exclude it. sub_0020E547, the crash caller that appeared to have zero callers, is simply the jne target inside sub_0020E520 at 0x0020E53F, reached when byte [esi+0x1a] != 1. DISCARDED THIS ROUND: the memcpy-clone hypothesis - the only bulk copy in the registration chain is at 0x0022367D in sub_002235D0 and it is a strcat over a stack buffer, not a descriptor copy. Discriminator found: every ctor-stamped object has f4=00000001 while both failing ones have f4=18000001, and the ctor computes f4=(old & 0xFF000001)|1, so their prior top byte was 0x18 - a value none of the constructed objects had. Probes stripped, rebuilt, unchanged at 434/92/415.

message: Identified [desc+0x20]: it is a base-class pointer adjustment and -1 is the not-a-base sentinel, so it is correct data rather than corruption. The caller's zero-only guard catches a clean cast failure (0+0) but misses this one (0+-1)
note: Method borrowed from a Ghidra tutorial the user shared - recognise the construct rather than chase the value. The field is ADDED in sub_0020E547 (edi = vcall_result + [esi+0x20]) and SUBTRACTED in sub_002041D0 (esi = esi - [eax+0x20], ledger #143's this-desc[0x20] idiom). Added one way and subtracted the other is a base-subobject displacement carried in a type descriptor, and MSVC RTTI uses -1 as the not-present marker. REFUTES two of my own readings recorded earlier today: 'heap residue nothing ever wrote' and 'an unfinished object'. The guest watchpoint had already refuted the first by reporting MISSED WRITES with the field actually holding FFFFFFFF; this explains what the value means. The failure shape: a dynamic-cast asks for a base pointer then adjusts by the displacement; a clean miss gives 0+0=0 and the caller's je catches it, while this gives 0+(-1)=-1 which is non-zero and passes into a dereference. So the descriptor is fine and the type system is correctly saying the types are unrelated - the fault is upstream, in a registry that does not know the relationship. Same incompletely-populated registry as the ready-flag flip and the [desc+0x3c] forwarding chain.

message: ROOT CAUSE: the descriptor is entirely uninitialised. Its instance size (+0x48) and allocation prefix (+0x20) are BOTH -1, so the create path asks the allocator for 0xFFFFFFFE bytes, gets NULL, and computes this = 0 + (-1) = -1. One fault, not two - the allocator is behaving correctly
note: Ghidra made this findable in a few queries. FUN_0020e520 is create-an-instance: allocate desc->size48 + desc->prefix20 through the context's vtable slot 0xCC, hand back raw+prefix, initialise via FUN_002096b0. Slot 0xCC is a thunk (sub_001EC5E0) forwarding to slot 0x1AC, which is sub_00211530 - a full MSVC-style debug heap. Probing every one of its 235 calls: the healthy ones use ctx=01088A90 with sane sizes (0xC, 0x10, 0x34...), and the LAST call before the crash is ctx=01218000 size=FFFFFFFE. Since size = field_48 + prefix and prefix = -1, field_48 is -1 too. The allocator is asked for ~4GB, correctly fails, returns 0. REFUTES my own framing from earlier today that this was 'two independent faults' and that 'a failing allocator during type registration is worth chasing on its own merits' - there is no allocator bug, and the budget check is not involved either: probed +0x98 limit = FFFFFFFF and +0x9C nolimit = FFFFFFFF, so the budget path is bypassed entirely. Also ruled out: FUN_001f5c20, the fallback allocator-context getter that reads the 0x005BB700 subsystem registry, is never called this run (zero probe hits), so the empty registry is not implicated here. Single root cause: a descriptor that never ran its constructor, arriving from the +0x3c forwarding chain. Probes stripped, rebuilt, unchanged at 434/92/415.

message: Traced the bad descriptor to an owner object's field, and refuted my own +0x3c forwarding-chain explanation: fwd is 0 on every descriptor, so that loop never runs. The descriptor arrives already broken, passed in as [owner+0x38] by sub_0020E960
note: REFUTES the previous entry's claim that the descriptor 'arrives from the +0x3c forwarding chain'. Probe [CHAIN] on sub_0020E520 entry across 18 calls shows fwd[+0x3c]=00000000 for ALL descriptors including the fatal one, so the while loop is never entered. The descriptor is simply the ecx argument, already carrying size48=FFFFFFFF prefix20=FFFFFFFF. Backtrace names the immediate caller sub_0020E960+0x243, whose disassembly shows 'mov ecx,[edi+0x38]; push eax; call 0x20e520' - so the descriptor comes from an owner object's field. Probe [OWNER] over 37 calls: every owner shares vtable 0x003F7EA0, healthy ones point at registered descriptors (01097498, 01097518, 01091AB0, 01096BB8) and the fatal owner 010982C8 points at the unregistered 01098358. Two constructors write that vtable. sub_0021B060 is a COPY constructor that copies +0x38 from another instance - probed, runs ZERO times this boot. sub_0021C3F0 is the default constructor and sets +0x38 to NULL (param_1[0xe]=0). So the owner starts with a null descriptor and something ASSIGNS 0x01098358 afterwards; that assignment is the remaining unknown. Guest watchpoint on 0x010982C8+0x38 reported MISSED WRITES - it saw 8 writes, none installing the value, and the field ends holding it, so its page-unprotect window is hiding the write. Probes stripped, rebuilt, unchanged at 434/92/415.

message: The wall traces back to BLOCKER_005BB700 after all: the subsystem registry count is 1, so the type lookup's fallback to a previously-registered subsystem is dead code. Found with a new software watchpoint poll that catches writes the page watchpoint cannot
note: NEW INSTRUMENT: xbox_WatchPoll / xbox_WatchPollVA read the watched dword after every recompiled call and report a change with the callee's name and a backtrace. Built because the page-protection watchpoint reported MISSED WRITES twice - it cannot see a write that lands while the page is unprotected, which it must be while a faulting instruction retires. The poll is slow and cannot be fooled. It found the write in three hits where the page watchpoint found nothing: guest 0x01098300 changed 00000000 -> 01098358 across icall sub_001E9380. CHAIN: FUN_001e9380 is a type-descriptor lookup - return my table slot at [this + idx*0x90 + 0x14]; if empty and flag 0x4000000 is set, build it via vfunc 0xC8; otherwise fall back to the subsystem registered before me, which requires 1 < DAT_005bc544. Probed: regcount = 1, so the fallback is DEAD CODE. DAT_005bc544 is BLOCKER_005BB700's count and 0x5BB704 its table, which holds up to four subsystems; SubsystemRegistry_Register at 0x00216210 never runs because its only reference is DATA. CORRECTS my own entry from earlier today which said the registry was 'a real defect but not implicated in this crash' - that was based on FUN_001f5c20 never being called, but that is a DIFFERENT consumer of the same registry. Probes stripped, rebuilt, unchanged at 434/92/415, crash RVA 0xECD5C5.

message: Attempted a fix and it failed, cleanly: the wall is a BOOTSTRAP ORDERING problem, not a missing pool type. The registrar itself does the type lookup that fails, while creating the very first pool, before any slot is filled
note: Traced the failing lookup precisely. Probe [LOOK2] over 123 lookups: exactly ONE fails, idx=2 slot14=00000000 flags=00000000 regcount=1. Probe [SLOTS] shows why - at that lookup ALL EIGHT pool slots read 00000000, and at every later lookup they all read 01088A90. Probe [EARLY] with a backtrace shows the premature lookup comes from sub_00216251, which is INSIDE SubsystemRegistry_Register: while constructing the very first memory pool it calls vfunc 0x58, which calls back into the type lookup for type 2 before any slot has been stored. The registrar's own loop then fills slots 1-3 and 8+ by copying slot 0, and 4-7 with their own pools. On hardware the lookup's fallback to a PREVIOUSLY REGISTERED subsystem covers this bootstrap window; here only one subsystem ever registers (probe [REGISTER]: exactly one invocation, this=01087000, count 0 -> 1), so 1 < count is false and the fallback is dead. FAILED EXPERIMENT, recorded because the negative is worth as much as the positive: 0x005BC51C is a char* the registrar strcmps against igArenaMemoryPool and igMallocMemoryPool to choose a pool class, and it has 5 readers and 0 writers - a genuinely uninitialised global. Set it to igMallocMemoryPool in recomp_manual.c next to the TLS-index fix. Verified the write landed (probe [POOLNAME]: ptr=003F5C68, first bytes igMa) and the outcome was IDENTICAL - 434/92/415 and the same crash - because all three branches call the same vfunc 0x58 before allocating, so the pool type does not avoid the bootstrap lookup at all. REVERTED rather than left in: no measured benefit and no evidence the game wants the malloc pool. Baseline verified restored at 434/92/415, crash RVA 0xECD5C5.

message: Closed three avenues by measurement without moving the wall: the failed icalls are all garbage rather than missing functions, g_IsEngineRunning is faithful, and the software poll attributes a write to a whole call subtree rather than pinpointing it
note: NEGATIVE RESULTS, recorded so they are not re-run. (1) FAILED ICALLS ARE SYMPTOMS, NOT CAUSES: 271 distinct unresolved targets, 105 in the code range, and applying the prologue-and-not-inside-a-known-function filter that found the 512 data pointers leaves exactly ONE survivor - 0x0012BA6B, which is unaligned and preceded by real code, so mid-function. The rest are null-derived garbage (0, 1, 2, 0x394, 0xCCCCCCCC, and patterns like 0x0003FFE3 / 0x0007FFE3 / 0x000FFFE3). Separately all 512 plausibility-filter rejects are outside the code range entirely, so the filter is not eating real calls. Seeding will not help this wall. (2) g_IsEngineRunning at 0x005BC548 is set to 1 by sub_00011E40 at 0x00011E60, before the registrar runs, so the registrar's engine-already-running branches are faithful - which is why all eight pool slots hold the same pool. Not a defect. (3) CORRECTS MY OWN ATTRIBUTION: the [WATCH-POLL] instrument fires after a call RETURNS, so it attributes a change to that call's entire dynamic subtree. Reporting the write as 'across icall sub_001E9380' bounds the region; it does not name the writer. sub_001E9380 can return 0 (flags=0, slot empty, regcount=1 so the fallback is dead) while something deeper in its subtree writes owner+0x38. The writer is still unidentified. Failed pool-type experiment from the previous entry remains reverted. Baseline unchanged at 434/92/415, crash RVA 0xECD5C5.

message: Chain complete: -1 is the constructor's 'size unknown' marker, and sub_00216FD0 fills the real size during type registration. The fatal descriptor is manufactured by the lookup path instead of found among the registered types, so it never reaches the filler
note: Watched a HEALTHY descriptor's size field (0x01097498+0x48) with the software poll and got both writes with backtraces. Write 1, 00000000 -> FFFFFFFF, from sub_00216EE0+0x2e3 - the descriptor constructor itself writes -1 as 'size not yet known', under sub_00222708. Write 2, FFFFFFFF -> 00000010, from sub_00216FD0+0x741 under sub_002235D0 -> sub_002225B0 - the registration driver filling the real size. So -1 is a deliberate marker, not residue, and the fatal descriptor simply never reaches write 2. WHY: the 7 healthy descriptors are built by sub_00222708 and then sized by registration; 01098358 is manufactured by the LOOKUP path (FUN_002226e0 with the registry ready-flag set, calling sub_0020E520 to create an instance of the descriptor type) and nothing sizes it afterwards. Also checked and cleared this round: the class-construct vfunc at slot 0x24 resolves and IS lifted for every object (0013D370 for the descriptor class, 001EAED0 for the owner class), so no failed icall is involved - and sub_0013D370 is an empty function, which is why construction alone never sets the size. The vtable being NULL at sub_002096B0 entry is also faithful: its first statement installs the vtable from [desc+0x5c] at the offset in [registry+0x394]. Probes stripped, rebuilt, unchanged at 434/92/415, crash RVA 0xECD5C5.

message: Found the ordering: sub_00236500 sets the registry ready-flag after the FIRST type-module registration and before the other ~24, so every later registration takes the create-instance path and produces a blank descriptor that registration must then fill
note: Watched the ready flag at [0x5BC508]+0 (guest 0x01086000) with the software poll: it flips 0 -> 1 exactly once, in straight-line code inside sub_002366BC, a fragment of sub_00236500, and the decompilation shows the sequence plainly - FUN_00209650(&LAB_002221e0) runs with the flag clear, then '*param_1 = 1', then roughly 24 further FUN_00209650 registrations run with it set. That is the ORIGINAL's own sequence, so it must work on hardware: the create-instance path is expected to hand back a blank descriptor which the registration then populates, and sub_00216FD0 is the function that populates the size. It does so for descriptors reached through sub_002235D0. The fatal one is reached through sub_00223960 -> FUN_002226e0 and stored by sub_002263F0, which sets owner+0x34=1 but never sizes it. sub_00223960 caches in DAT_005bc1ac, which is BSS and null, so the type it wants was not registered during the flag-clear window. DAT_0046a684 is 6, a pool index rather than a type name, so the type is not identifiable from that argument. NOT YET ANSWERED: why descriptors reached via sub_002263F0 are never sized while those via sub_002235D0 are. Probes stripped, rebuilt, unchanged at 434/92/415, crash RVA 0xECD5C5.

message: WALL BROKEN: 434 -> 514 kernel calls, callsites 415 -> 435, heap 92 -> 94, and the crash moves from sub_002096B0+0xd5 to sub_001EA600+0x2c3. An unsized type descriptor now behaves as a clean instantiation failure instead of producing the pointer -1
note: Deterministic 2 of 2 at 514 kernel / 94 heap / 435 callsites, crash RVA 0xDE0703 = sub_001EA600+0x2c3, fault 0xD3010000. THE GUARD, one line in sub_0020E547 after 'edi = edi + ebx': if (ebx == 0xFFFFFFFFu) { edi = 0; }. ebx is the descriptor prefix from [esi+0x20] and the allocator is asked for [esi+0x48] + ebx. A descriptor created but not yet sized carries -1 in both, so the request is 0xFFFFFFFE, the allocator correctly returns NULL, and the line computes 0 + (-1) = -1 - non-zero, so the following je lets it through and sub_002096B0 writes through -1. With a sized descriptor the same failure gives 0 + 0 = 0 and the je catches it, so the guard restores the behaviour that je was written for rather than inventing one. This is the walls.py method - try a bypass, measure - and it is a BYPASS not a fix: the real defect is that descriptors reached via sub_002263F0 are never sized, which is unchanged and still documented as open. Persisted into manual_edits.json so it survives regeneration; verify reports 1068/1068 placed. CAUTION WORTH RECORDING: running 'manual_edits.py extract' rewrote the store with 1061 entries against 1067 held, silently dropping 6 edits that exist in the store but not in current gen. Restored from git and added the single entry surgically instead. Do not blind-extract after a regeneration or a probe sweep.

message: SECOND WALL: guarding an unfilled field slot advances callsites 435 -> 445 and moves the crash to sub_001EB890+0x1d5. Same defect class one layer up - a type's field array has a count covering slots registration never filled
note: Deterministic 2 of 2 at 514 kernel / 94 heap / 445 callsites, crash RVA 0xDED4C5 = sub_001EB890+0x1d5, fault 0x8B0146F4. FUN_001ea600 walks a type's fields calling vfunc 0x74 on each: ebx+0xC is the count, ebx+8 the array. At the crash esi=4 with count 6, and field[4] read 0xD3000000 - the array is sized for 6 but registration filled only the inherited 4, so the next line dereferenced garbage for the vtable. GUARD: skip a slot whose pointer is outside [0x00880000, 0x04000000), the same range sub_0020E547 already uses in this tree for the same judgement, jumping to the loop increment. This is the guard-uninitialised-X bypass class already proven here (ledger #1-#3). Kernel calls flat at 514 - expected, since the narrow proxy does not move for a guard that only skips work - while callsites rose 10 and the crash site changed, which is the spin-proof signal. Persisted; manual_edits verify reports 1069/1069. STILL OPEN and unchanged by either bypass: type descriptors reached via sub_002263F0 are never sized, and their field arrays are never populated. Both walls broken today are symptoms of that one defect.

message: Wall 42 diagnosed, not guarded: sub_001EB890 is passed an object that is not a string table at all. Its count field holds a pointer and its array field holds 0x680 - the caller's field 0 is bogus, so this is the same under-populated-object defect presenting a third way
note: Probed the table shape across all 135 calls. The healthy ones read base=01091B30 count=0x41 start=0x40 array=01091B50 - sane and growing. The fatal one reads base=0109863C count=0x01096D04 start=0x01092B54 array=0x00000680: the count is a POINTER and the array is a small integer, so the object is not a string table. FUN_001eb890 is a binary search over a sorted string table and FUN_001f87a0 removes an entry from one, so this IS supposed to be a table; FUN_0020ef90 passes *(void**)this, its own field 0, which therefore holds the wrong pointer. DELIBERATELY NOT GUARDED: the previous two walls were containers sized but unpopulated, where skipping an entry restores an existing check's intent. This one is a wrong object, and a range check would paper over a propagated bad pointer rather than restore anything - the useful fix is upstream, at whatever leaves field 0 unset. Baseline verified clean after stripping probes at 514 kernel / 94 heap / 445 callsites, crash RVA 0xDED4C5.

message: Wall 42 root cause found: the holder object at 01092B58 is not under-populated, its table pointer is OVERWRITTEN between uses. sub_0020AA90 (the allocator free path) changes holder+0 from 01091B30 to 0109863C
note: Chain established with the guest watchpoint. RECOMP_WATCH=0x01092B58 gave two poll hits: 00000000 -> 01091B30 (population), then 01091B30 -> 0109863C across sub_0020AA90. Backtrace for hit 2: sub_0020EF90+0x22c -> sub_0020EEE0 -> sub_001EC750 -> sub_00211530 (allocator). FUN_00123600 is a refcount release - it decrements param_1[1] and calls FUN_0020ef90 when it reaches zero. FUN_0020ef90 removes the entry from the table and then, when holder+0x20 is nonzero, calls FUN_0020eee0(*this, this) which reallocates/shrinks and stores a new table pointer back into holder+0. The replacement pointer is the bogus one. Watching holder+0x20 showed it set 0 -> 1 by sub_001F8830 under sub_00216EE0, the descriptor constructor, so the auto-release flag is legitimate initialisation and NOT the defect. Deliberately not guarded: the object is wrong, not merely unfilled, and the rule stands - restore a check the original wrote, never invent one to survive bad data.

message: Wall 42 re-diagnosed: it is a USE-AFTER-FREE of the holder at 01092B58, not a corrupted table pointer. [AMENDED 2026-09-02: the recursion explanation in this entry is RETRACTED - see the retraction at the end of the note. The use-after-free stands; the reason the holder is released three times does not]
note: Counters unchanged and deterministic 2 of 2 at 514 kernel / 445 callsites, crash sub_001EB890+0x1d5, fault 0x8B0146F4. DIAGNOSIS ONLY - no guard applied. The previous entry's mechanism was wrong and is superseded. Evidence: (1) FUN_0020AA90 is a dlmalloc free - it decodes a chunk header at param_1-4, pushes onto a small bin with *(chunk+4)=bin[(size>>3)-1], coalesces and trims. The watched write is that free-list link landing in the freed block. (2) FUN_0020EEE0 does not realloc/shrink; it unlinks a list node and FREES its param_1 via getContainingMemoryPool(param_1)->vtbl+0xFC. FUN_0020EF90 passes its own `this` as that param_1, so it frees the holder. (3) Entry probe on FUN_0020EF90: this=01092B58 on all three calls with flag=01 each time; field0 reads 01091B30, 01091B30, then 0109863C. (4) Software poll on 0x01092B58 named the writer: '01091B30 -> 0109863C across sub_0020AA90'. The page-protection watchpoint reported 33 hits of 00000000 on the same address and emitted MISSED WRITES - its log was untrustworthy exactly as documented, and it briefly produced a wrong conclusion. (5) recomp_where stacks: all three calls enter via sub_00123600+0xC9 -> sub_00217FF0+0xD6, and the frame pair sub_001EA640+0x67B / sub_001F8180+0x9F repeats verbatim - call #1 at depth 0, #2 at depth 1, #3 at depth 2. One recursive walk releasing the same holder once per level. (6) FUN_001EA640 is a generic metafield teardown: it takes the object's meta via vtbl+0x50, reads _metaFields at meta+0x28, iterates from igObject_Meta's own field count to meta_fields[0xC], and dispatches per field kind. Count at +0xC and array at +8 is the same structure wall 41 was about, which ties 42 to the same unpopulated-metaobject root cause rather than a separate defect. STILL OPEN: whether the field list is malformed so the walk visits the holder twice, or the recursion is legitimate and the release is premature. That decides where the fix goes and needs sub_001F8180 read. NOT GUARDED - guarding a read of freed memory would hide a use-after-free. ||| RETRACTION, same day, appended rather than rewritten so the record shows what was believed and why it fell. Points (5) and (6) above are WITHDRAWN. A WENTER probe on FUN_001EA640 shows it is entered only 4 times in the entire boot, on 4 different objects, and NONE of them is the holder 01092B58. It therefore cannot be the recursive walk that releases the holder once per level, and it is not on wall 42's path at all.
